line_ref_convention: 行号为 text/ch07_chapter_7.txt 的 1 基行号；引文逐字抄录
pov: 海伦娜（第三人称限知，含童年闪回 L53–L73）

events.did: 立刻希望收回刚才的话；向辛西娅承认自己的力量让她本能地觉得不对
events.verbatim: Helena immediately wished she could call back her words. Admitting her powers to Cynthia felt intrinsically wrong.

events.did: 自幼靠三条不可打破的规则活着：不向血亲与巫团以外的人显露力量；不信任血亲与巫团以外的人；不愛血亲与巫团以外的人
events.verbatim: Since childhood, she had lived by three unbreakable rules: Don’t reveal your powers to anyone outside of kin and coven. Don’t trust anyone outside of kin and coven. Don’t love anyone outside of kin and coven.

events.did: 刚对辛西娅打破了一条规则；但当那女人倾身发问、榛色眼睛像暗森林般神秘、香草与忍冬像某种爱情咒从她身上倾泻，海伦娜失去了理智
events.verbatim: She just broke one of her rules with Cynthia. But when the woman leaned forward to ask her question, hazel eyes as mysterious as a dark forest, vanilla and honeysuckle pouring from her like some kind of love spell, Helena lost all sense.

events.did: 闪过上次信任外人时的禁忌记忆：她从家里逃出、从母亲身边逃开，血顺着手臂滴下；温柔的母亲已变成别的什么东西——可怕而扭曲；她在不平的土路上踉跄、拼命迈动小短腿；罗恩姨妈家离林中小屋十五分钟路程，她大约跑五分钟就到，但到时罗恩姨妈不在
events.verbatim: A forbidden memory of the last time she trusted an outsider flashed in her mind. Helena was running from her home, running from her mother as blood dripped down her arm. Her sweet, gentle mother had become something else. Something terrifying and twisted. Helena stumbled on the uneven dirt path as she pumped her little legs harder. Aunt Rowan’s was a fifteen-minute walk from their cottage in the woods; surely she could run there in five. But when she got there, Aunt Rowan was gone.

events.did: 推断「村子……她一定是被叫到村子里去了」
events.verbatim: ‘The village… she must have been called to the village.’

events.who: 海伦娜（童年）与老坎贝尔太太
events.did: 她从空气中抽水，在恐惧加持下以更强大的力量之浪冲上前；差点撞上老坎贝尔太太；坎贝尔太太看见一个女孩踩着一条水河、水河瞬间如雾消失，吓得瞪大眼，在她摔倒前接住了她
events.verbatim: She pulled the water from the air and rushed forward on a wave of power made even more potent by her fear. She nearly crashed into Old Mrs Campbell. Her eyes widened at the sight of a girl running on a river of water that disappeared like mist in a moment. She caught Helena before she could fall.

events.did: 问「你在流血，小姑娘。到底怎么了？」（苏格兰方言）
events.verbatim: ‘Yer bleeding’, lass. What the devil is wrong?’

events.did: 在纯粹的慌乱中把一切都告诉了坎贝尔太太；而这一场倾诉摧毁了她整个世界
events.verbatim: In her sheer panic, she told Mrs Campbell everything, and in the telling, destroyed her entire world.

events.did: 说「您脸色发白，小姐。您还好吗？」
events.verbatim: ‘You’ve gone pale, Miss Blair. Are you well?’

events.did: 眨眼驱散禁忌记忆，挤出僵硬的笑，无视辛西娅眼中的关切——她最不需要的是一个可能面对绞刑的女人的怜悯；回「我很好。倒该担心的是你。如果你藏了什么秘密，你的念头会出卖你，伯罗斯夫人。」
events.verbatim: Helena blinked, dispelling the forbidden memory. She forced a brittle smile, ignoring the concern in Cynthia’s gaze. The last thing she needed was pity from a woman facing the possibility of a hangman’s noose. ‘I’m perfectly fine. It’s you who should be worried. If you’re keeping any secrets, your thoughts will betray you, Lady Burrows.’

events.did: 挑眉；海伦娜看到她脉搏在颌下细腻皮肤上狂跳；关切很快被挑战取代，今日她的眼睛绿色多于棕色；反问「我现在在想什么秘密，布莱尔小姐？」
events.verbatim: Cynthia’s eyebrows winged up. Helena saw the flutter of her pulse beat madly against the delicate skin just under her jaw. Concern was quickly replaced by the flash of challenge in Cynthia’s eyes, more green than brown today. ‘What secrets am I thinking now, Miss Blair?’

events.did: 挪动身体，椅子吱呀作响，提醒海伦娜她不是与辛西娅独处；整个世界再次消失只剩两人；海伦娜自问是什么黑暗魔法在作祟，让自己忘掉一切只剩辛西娅柔软的声音与尖锐的问题——而她答不上来，因为她完全不知道辛西娅脑中在跑什么念头
events.verbatim: Uncle Lachlan shifted, the creaking of his chair reminding Helena that she wasn’t alone with Cynthia. Once again, the entire world had disappeared until it was just the two of them. What dark magic was at play that Helena would forget everything except Cynthia’s soft voice and sharp questions? Questions that Helena could not answer. Because she had no clue what thoughts ran riot in Cynthia’s mind.

events.did: 「Damn her for testing me!」（她在测试我）
events.verbatim: Damn her for testing me!

events.did: 在尴尬地承认真相之前转为进攻：「你从没归还吊坠。它是案子的证物。我们得拿回来。」
events.verbatim: Before she embarrassed herself by admitting the truth, she pivoted to the attack. ‘You never returned the locket. It’s evidence in the case. We’ll need it back.’

events.did: 回「你从没问我要我还」，把手伸进裙褶取出那件要命的珠宝，让它从指间垂下，红宝石在阳光下闪光；并说「我昨天骗了你」
events.verbatim: ‘You never asked me to return it.’ Cynthia slipped her hand in a fold of her skirt, pulling free the damning jewellery. She let it dangle from her fingers, the rubies glinting in the sunlight. ‘I lied to you yesterday.’

events.did: 「不可能！」警觉传遍全身；她一向知道谁在说谎——直到现在；追问「你是在承认你没说真话？」
events.verbatim: Impossible! Alarm winged through Helena. She always knew when someone lied. Until now. ‘You are admitting that you didn’t tell us the truth?’

events.did: 澄清「我承认的是我不知道真相，因此误导了你们」
events.verbatim: ‘I’m admitting that I didn’t know the truth, and thus inadvertently misled you.’

events.who: 拉奇兰叔叔（苏格兰方言）
events.did: 说「伯罗斯小姐，恕我直言，但你这是在搞什么？向苏格兰场警长撒谎在谋杀案里对你可没什么好处。」
events.verbatim: ‘Miss Burrows, you’ll pardon my bluntness, but what the hell are ye on abou’? Lying to the Superintendent of Scotland Yard hardly bodes well for ye in a murder case.’

events.did: 回「在我的谎言把我自己牵连进谋杀时例外，真相会帮我脱身」；她的得意笑容在海伦娜胸口击碎某种坚硬冰冷的东西
events.verbatim: ‘Not when my lie implicated me in his murder, and the truth will help to set me free.’ Cynthia’s triumphant smile cracked something hard and cold around Helena’s chest.

events.did: 按下吊坠边缘，吊坠弹开，里面是两张微型画像；海伦娜凑近，蜷在她身侧的哈姆雷特好奇地歪头
events.verbatim: She pressed the edge of the locket, and it sprang open. Inside were two miniature portraits. Helena leaned closer. Hamlet, who was curled next to her side, cocked his head in interest.

events.did: 说「这不是我的项链」并把证物递给海伦娜，「至少现在不是了」
events.verbatim: ‘This is not my necklace.’ Cynthia offered the evidence to Helena. ‘At least, not any more.’

events.did: 从她手中抢过吊坠，眯眼看那两张脸；说「那是你丈夫」，拇指抚过休伯特的小像
events.verbatim: Snatching it from her hand, she squinted at the two faces within. ‘That is your husband.’ Helena brushed her thumb over a miniature of Lord Hubert.

events.did: 确认「是的，但对面那个女人肯定不是我」
events.verbatim: ‘Yes, but the woman opposite is most certainly not me.’

events.did: 起身、跨过房间，从侄女手中拿过项链，说「我不明白」
events.verbatim: Superintendent MacDougal stood, strode across the room on powerful legs, and took the necklace from his niece. ‘I don’t understand.’

events.did: 说「他十多年前把这个吊坠给我时，我的脸在他对面」
events.verbatim: ‘When he gave me that locket, more than ten years ago, my face was opposite his.’

events.did: 深褐色眼睛变锐利：「他把你的吊坠送给了别人。你认得这个女人吗？」
events.verbatim: Uncle Lachlan’s dark-brown eyes sharpened. ‘He gave your locket to someone else. Do you recognise this woman?’

events.did: 笑动摇；说不认得；猜那是丈夫某一个情妇，「也许这位女士特别合他口味。又或者那小玩意对他来说跟我一样无足轻重」
events.verbatim: Cynthia’s smile faltered. ‘No. I don’t. I suppose it could be any number of his mistresses. I’m no idiot. I know my husband philandered with all manner of women. Perhaps this lady caught his particular fancy. Or mayhap the trinket meant as little to him as I did. It’s hard to say.’

events.did: 愤怒如 rogue wave 涌起；他怎敢如此冷漠地对待妻子——把求爱期送她的礼物转给情妇是蓄意残忍；她也许不喜欢辛西娅，但没有女人该被丈夫这样羞辱
events.verbatim: Anger rose in Helena like a rogue wave. How dare he treat his wife with such callous disregard? To take a gift he’d given her in their courtship to a mistress was wilfully cruel. She might not like Cynthia, but no woman deserved to be humiliated by her husband in such a manner.

events.did: 问「他身上会不会有能帮我们找到这位……呃，朋友的物品？」脸颊变深，显然在艰难地谈论侯爵明目张胆的不忠
events.verbatim: ‘Would he have anything in his possession that might aid us in locating this, er, friend of his?’ Uncle Lachlan’s cheeks darkened. He was clearly struggling to talk around the awkwardness of Lord Burrows’ blatant infidelity.

events.did: 耸肩，端起茶杯却没喝；手在颤出卖她的紧张；「他房间里有保险箱。我们可以从那里开始。」
events.verbatim: Shrugging, Cynthia lifted her teacup to her lips but didn’t sip. The tremor in her hand betrayed her nerves. This wasn’t as easy as she was pretending. ‘He has a safe in his room. We could start there.’

events.did: 问「钥匙在你手上吗？」并站起；哈姆雷特跳下来期待地等在她身边
events.verbatim: ‘Do you have the key?’ Helena stood. Hamlet hopped down, waiting expectantly next to her.

events.did: 脆笑作答「几乎没有。但他的贴身男仆知道钥匙在哪。我让他帮忙收拾休伯特的东西。走。」她起身优雅地走出房间；三人跟进门厅、上宽大楼梯到三楼、沿挂着画像的长廊走；最后一幅画是休伯特与辛西娅，必定是婚后不久委托的；画家技艺高超，捕捉到辛西娅榛色眼中的希望与休伯特笑容里的傲慢占有
events.verbatim: Cynthia’s brittle laughter answered the question. ‘Hardly. But his valet will know where he kept it. I asked him to help pack Hubert’s things. Come.’ She stood and gracefully swept out of the room. Helena and Uncle Lachlan followed her into the hall, up the wide stairwell to the third floor, then down a long corridor with portraits lining the wall. The last painting was of Hubert and Cynthia. It must have been commissioned soon after their wedding. The artist was skilled at his craft. He captured the hope blazing in Cynthia’s hazel eyes. And the smug ownership in Hubert’s smile.

events.did: 对这个死者的恨意更深了
events.verbatim: Helena’s hatred for the dead man grew.

events.did: 辛西娅打开走廊尽头的门并猛然停住；海伦娜撞上她、抓住她的髋部稳住两人——这是无意识的反应，但身体碰撞让海伦娜产生强烈觉知
events.verbatim: Cynthia opened the door at the end of the hall and juddered to a halt. Helena ran into her, grabbing Cynthia’s hips to steady them both. It was an unconscious reaction, but acute awareness pulsed through Helena as their bodies collided.

events.did: 低声咒骂
events.verbatim: Uncle Lachlan cursed low and foul.

events.did: 一个年轻男人，圆礼帽压低遮眼、不合身的西装掩住身形，手里拿着刚从墙上取下的画像，站住不动；画后面是休伯特保险箱的钢光；男仆坐在地上，双手被绑在背后、嘴里塞着东西，看到他们在门口便开始剧烈挣扎并发出声响
events.verbatim: A young man, bowler hat pulled low over his eyes, poorly fitting suit hiding his shape, froze. He was holding a painting he’d just removed from the wall. Behind the painting was the steel glint of Hubert’s safe. The valet sat on the floor. His hands were tied behind his back, and a gag was in his mouth. When he saw them standing in the doorway, he began making a concerted and frantic racket while writhing to escape.

events.did: 大喊「别动！」
events.verbatim: ‘Don’t move!’ Uncle Lachlan shouted.

events.did: 「他妈的！要是没把东西带回去，魔鬼肯定要我的命。」
events.verbatim: Fucking hell! The Devil’s going to kill me for sure if I come back without it.

events.did: 窃贼的念头太响，她退缩了一下
events.verbatim: The thief’s thoughts were so loud, Helena flinched.

events.did: 把画像朝他们扔来，以惊人的运动能力冲过房间、跑向开着的窗户、窜了出去
events.verbatim: The man threw the painting at them. With admirable athleticism, he raced across the room to the open window and scuttled out.

events.did: 叔叔跳过破碎的画像冲到窗边，海伦娜紧随其后
events.verbatim: Uncle Lachlan leapt over the broken painting and hurried to the window, Helena on his heels.

events.did: 那年轻小子以极快速度沿砖墙下爬，她赶到窗边时他几乎已落地；她聚起力量掷出一道水浪把他掀过修剪整齐的草坪 inadvertently 帮了他的忙；他站稳后钻进树篱，她来不及发起第二次攻击
events.verbatim: The young lad scaled down the brick wall with such speed, he was almost on the ground by the time Helena reached the window. She pooled her powers, throwing a blast of water that tumbled the boy across the manicured lawn, inadvertently aiding his escape. He recovered his feet and dove through the hedges before she could lobby a second attack.

events.did: 骂「该死！」；这感觉像输，她不喜欢输
events.verbatim: ‘Blasted hell!’ This felt like losing, and she didn’t like losing.

events.did: 冲进走廊大喊求援，脚步声砰砰下楼
events.verbatim: Uncle Lachlan turned and rushed into the hall, yelling for assistance as his footsteps pounded down the stairs.

events.did: 知道没有她拖累叔叔更有把握抓住那小子，便从窗边转身去查看窃贼是否打开了保险箱
events.verbatim: Knowing Uncle Lachlan had a far better chance of catching the lad without Helena slowing him down, she turned from the window to assess whether the thief had managed to open the safe.

events.did: 辛西娅蹲在男仆旁边挣扎着解他手腕上的绳子；哈姆雷特坐在她旁边嗅那人的耳朵，那人瑟缩
events.verbatim: Cynthia crouched on the floor next to the valet and struggled with the rope binding his wrists together. Hamlet sat next to her. He sniffed the valet’s ear as the poor man flinched away.

events.did: 对男仆说「他不会伤害你，劳伦斯。他是一只可爱的狐狸，对吧？」并朝哈姆雷特甜甜一笑；狐狸龇牙后她改口「他是一只狂野而可怕的生物，不会伤害你，因为他有令人印象的自制力」
events.verbatim: ‘He won’t hurt you, Lawrence. He’s a lovely fox, aren’t you?’ Cynthia spared Hamlet a sweet smile. The fox curled his lip in a snarl. ‘Ah. Right. Sorry. He’s a wild and fearsome creature who won’t hurt you because of his impressive self-control.’

events.did: 拒绝被辛西娅迷住
events.verbatim: Helena refused to be charmed by Cynthia.

events.did: 海伦娜蹲下处理塞在男仆牙间的口塞——拧成条的枕套，强行塞进牙间又绕头绑住；问「你可怜的人！发生了什么？」；海伦娜解开枕套的结时，辛西娅正好松开他手腕上的绳子；男仆扯掉口塞、揉着磨破的手腕
events.verbatim: Joining the woman, she crouched down and worked on the gag, which appeared to be a pillowcase twisted and forced between his teeth, then tied around his head. ‘You poor man! What happened?’ Cynthia asked. Helena untied the knot in the pillowcase just as Cynthia was able to loosen the rope around his wrists. The valet helped pull the gag away and rubbed his raw wrists.

events.did: 叙述：他在大勋爵的 closet 里听见 scuffling，出来查看，那个杂种就站在那里、手枪顶着他胸口；那男人让他拿保险箱钥匙并把他绑起来，威胁他出声就开枪；感谢上帝那男人为了取下画像收起了枪，否则他可能把你们俩都杀了；他说到此处眼睛瞪大、脸色发白
events.verbatim: ‘I was in his lordship’s closet when I heard scuffling. I came out to investigate and that bastard – pardon my language, Lady Burrows – but that bastard was standing there, a pistol pointing at my chest. He made me get the key to the safe and tied me up, telling me he’d shoot me if I made a sound. Thank God he put his pistol away to take down the painting. He could have killed you both.’ The valet’s eyes grew wide, his face paling.

events.did: 越过男仆的头顶看向海伦娜；她的眼睛是森林的所有颜色：绿叶配棕色脉络、金色条纹混合灰色；海伦娜可以花永恒去分类她确切的色调
events.verbatim: Cynthia looked over the valet’s head to Helena. Her eyes were all the colours of the forest. Green leaves with veins of brown. Golden streaks blending with grey. Helena could spend eternity categorising their exact shade.

events.did: 提醒「你叔叔在追那个罪犯！我们必须警告他那个人带着枪。」
events.verbatim: ‘Your uncle is chasing the culprit! We must warn him that the man is armed.’

events.did: 摇头：「拉奇兰叔叔能应付自己。这不是他第一次跟持枪的人交手。我也不知道他能不能抓住他，那个黑帮比蒸汽火车还快。」并在心里补：那人因任务失败而惊恐；他在休伯特的保险箱里找什么？
events.verbatim: Helena shook her head. ‘Uncle Lachlan can handle himself. It wouldn’t be the first time he’s fought an armed man. I don’t know if he’ll catch him, at any rate. The blackguard was faster than a steam train.’ And terrified for failing in his mission. But what had he been looking for in Lord Burrows’ safe?

events.did: 搜地板找钥匙；辛西娅掀起一层褶皱 triumph 地叫出声，手里举着钥匙；喊「万岁！他逃跑时一定掉下来了。」
events.verbatim: ‘Did he take the key with him?’ Cynthia, the valet, and Helena searched the floor. Cynthia pulled up a ruffle and cried out in triumph, holding the key. ‘Huzzah! He must have dropped it when he fled.’

events.did: 辛西娅的快乐有感染力，但她拒绝被带动；辛西娅仍是丈夫谋杀案的首要嫌疑人，无论她脸颊因愉悦泛红时多么迷人，海伦娜最好别忘
events.verbatim: Her joy was infectious, but Helena refused to be swayed. Cynthia was still the lead suspect in her husband’s murder. A fact Helena best not forget, no matter how fetching she looked as her cheeks flushed with pleasure.

events.did: 走到保险箱前，小心插入设计用来开杠杆锁的 Chubb 钥匙；金属铰链咔嗒一声、吱呀作响，她拉开沉重的门；叹「哎呀。这可能要花些时间。」
events.verbatim: Cynthia stood and walked to the safe, carefully inserting the Chubb key designed to work the lever lock. With a clank and screech of metal hinges, she pulled open the heavy door. ‘Oh dear. This might take some time.’

events.did: 加入辛西娅往小隔间里看：塞满账簿、散纸、几个珠宝盒和一个上漆的珐琅盒；英勇地努力忽略从辛西娅身上散出的暖意；提议「我们应该等拉奇兰叔叔回来。」
events.verbatim: Helena joined her and peered into the small enclosure stuffed tight with ledgers, loose papers, several jewellery boxes, and a painted enamel case. Valiantly, she tried to ignore the warmth emanating from Cynthia. ‘We should wait until Uncle Lachlan returns.’

events.did: 从保险箱里抽出一本账簿，几张纸随之飘落；反问「你担心我篡改证据？」
events.verbatim: Cynthia reached into the safe and pulled a ledger free. Several papers fluttered to the floor in its wake. ‘Are you worried I might tamper with the evidence?’

events.did: 挑眉（这表情曾让许多男人落荒而逃）：「有罪的人能做出无穷无尽的背叛。」
events.verbatim: Helena raised her brow in an expression that had sent many a man running in fear. ‘A guilty person is capable of endless treachery.’

events.did: 幽默消逝：「那正好，我不是有罪。」转身面向海伦娜；两人靠得极近，海伦娜能数清辛西娅鼻梁上的肉桂色雀斑；「那就和我一起看。我怎么可能在你盯着我一举一动的情况下搞背叛？」火花回来了；「再说，你说我骗不了你。你会读我的念头、就会知道，那你还怕什么？」
events.verbatim: Cynthia’s humour died. ‘Then it’s a good thing I’m not guilty.’ She turned to face Helena. They were so close, Helena could count the cinnamon freckles on the bridge of Cynthia’s nose. ‘Look with me, then. How could I possibly embark on treachery if you are watching my every move?’ The sparkle was back. How she maintained such a positive attitude when her world was in tatters mystified Helena. ‘Besides, you said I couldn’t lie to you. You would read my thoughts and know, so what has you spooked?’

events.did: 「你。就是你让我害怕。」并抿紧嘴唇阻止话语溢出
events.verbatim: You. You have me spooked. Helena pressed her lips tight to keep the words from spilling forth.

events.did: 问「呃，如果你们不需要我，那我是不是下楼去？」——两个女人同时转向他：她们完全把他忘了
events.verbatim: ‘Err, should I just head downstairs then if you don’t need anything?’ Both women turned in tandem to the valet. Who they had forgotten entirely.

events.did: 让劳伦斯去告诉希金斯太太发生了什么、她会给他端杯茶；说麦克杜格尔警司回来后想跟他谈谈；说「不过你受了很大惊吓，茶对身体大有好处」；又补一句「听说白兰地也很能 restorative」
events.verbatim: Cynthia’s cheeks turned a delicate shade of pink. ‘Lawrence! Yes, of course. Why don’t you tell Mrs Higgins what has happened, and she’ll get you a cup of tea. When Superintendent MacDougal returns, I’m sure he’ll want to speak with you. But you’ve had a real shock, and tea does wonders for the constitution.’ She turned sharply to look at Hamlet, who flicked his fluffy tail. What the devil is going on with my familiar and Cynthia? Cynthia shook her head before looking back to the valet. ‘Brandy can also be quite restorative, I’ve heard.’

events.did: 翻另一页账簿；全是丈夫独特字迹写的惊人巨额款项；有些是分期、多数是取款；反复出现一组奇特的字母 DOSD；她判断休伯特欠这个神秘 DOSD 一大笔钱
events.verbatim: Cynthia flipped another page in a ledger full of entries written in her husband’s distinctive script. They were all staggering sums of money. While some were instalments, most were withdrawals. A curious combination of letters was repeated often. DOSD. Hubert owed the mysterious DOSD a very large amount indeed.

events.did: 低声骂「Bloody fucking hell」；完全不像淑女的措辞，但她此刻不想当淑女，只想当个彻底的蠢货；丈夫漏钱比筛子还快；她担心自己想象的寡妇生活已随休伯特一起完蛋
events.verbatim: ‘Bloody fucking hell,’ she muttered. Hardly the words of a lady. But she didn’t feel like a lady at this moment. She felt like a complete dunderhead. Her husband had been bleeding money faster than a sieve. She wasn’t sure what any of it meant, but she feared whatever comfortable living she imagined for her widowhood had gone to hell with Hubert.

events.did: 从一封信里抬头：「什么？」两人并排坐在地板上，纸片散在周围，辛西娅染得不好的裙子擦过海伦娜的蓝裙
events.verbatim: Helena looked up from a letter she was reading. ‘What?’ They were both sitting on the floor, with papers scattered around them. Cynthia’s poorly dyed skirts brushed against Helena’s blue ones.

events.did: 摇头：「就算我能证明清白，我也相信我算是毁了。」
events.verbatim: Cynthia shook her head. ‘Even if I can prove my innocence, I believe I’m quite ruined.’

events.did: 敲门、探头进来：「麦克杜格尔警司回来了。他想和你们两位谈谈。」辛西娅答「让他上来。他会想看这些。」
events.verbatim: A knock sounded on the door, and her butler ducked his head inside. ‘Superintendent MacDougal has returned. He desires to speak with both of you.’ ‘Send him up. He’ll want to see all of this.’ The butler nodded and quietly shut the door.

events.did: 说「也许这些不是现行的账簿。也可能是旧记录，他在你结婚前就还清了债」；挪动身体，肩膀撞上辛西娅的，一边探头看账簿
events.verbatim: ‘Perhaps these are not current ledgers. They could be old records, and he paid the debts before you were even married.’ Helena shifted so her shoulder bumped against Cynthia’s as she peered at the ledger.

events.did: 用手指点最后一笔的日期，清晰的字迹表明是三天前写的；回「我不这么认为」；并说若说服不了对方相信她清白，就不用操心住哪吃什么——在绞死之前，新门监狱负责她的食宿；她尖利地笑起来；她活在一场噩梦里，想醒来回到正常：丈夫没被杀、自己不面对刑期、就算活下来也不至于失去一切
events.verbatim: Cynthia tapped her finger on the date of the last entry. The clear script indicated it was penned three days prior. ‘I don’t think so. Well, I suppose if I can’t convince you of my innocence, I won’t have to worry about where to live or what to eat. Newgate will be in charge of my room and board until I hang for murder.’ She laughed, a high and shrill sound. Cynthia was living in a nightmare. She wanted to wake up and return to normalcy. A life where her husband was not murdered. Where she was not facing a prison sentence ending in her death. Where she didn’t risk losing everything if she did survive.

events.did: 窗外雷声隆隆，下午太阳躲进云后
events.verbatim: Thunder rumbled outside the window as the afternoon sun hid behind a cloud.

events.did: 「如果休伯特还活着，一切也不会不同。我仍会负债。我仍会被关在牢里。我仍会面对死亡，只是从缓慢的一点点变成一下子。」
events.verbatim: If Hubert was alive, nothing would be different. I would still be in debt. I would still be imprisoned. I would still be facing death, just in slow degrees instead of all at once.

events.did: 说「我不想你是有罪的，不管你怎么想。我也许不喜欢你，但我也不想你上绞架。我只是不能假定你无罪。」靠近，辛西娅一时冲动，怀疑女人的嘴唇是否比男人的更柔软
events.verbatim: ‘I don’t want you to be guilty, no matter what you think. I might not like you, but neither do I want you to hang. I just can’t assume you are innocent either.’ Helena leaned closer and for a reckless moment, Cynthia wondered if a woman’s lips were softer than a man’s.

events.did: 若注定要失去一切，抓住一根带电的线、让电流穿过自己直到只剩光，还有什么损失？因为每次碰到海伦娜就是那种感觉——像力量之流穿过她，让她感受到自己只能想象的东西
events.verbatim: If she was destined to lose everything, what harm might come from grabbing a live wire and letting the electricity run through her until she was nothing but light? Because whenever she touched Helena, that is how it felt. Like currents of power rushing through her, making her feel things she only ever imagined.

events.did: 「我打赌她尝起来像焦糖和盐。」紧接一句「她肯定不会像休伯特老那样带着雪茄与杜松子酒的味道。」
events.verbatim: I bet she tastes of caramel and salt. She certainly wouldn’t reek of cigars and gin as Hubert always had.

events.did: 猛然想起海伦娜能读心，意味着她知道自己刚才想的一切——那些最不愿承认的东西；结结巴巴「该死。你听到了……那个，也就是说，我并没有真的在想……」并说「闯进别人脑子里偷走念头，这可真够 cheeky 的，你知道。」
events.verbatim: Cynthia remembered in a horrible rush that Helena could read thoughts. Which meant she knew everything Cynthia had just been thinking. Things she most certainly didn’t want to admit. ‘Damnation. Did you hear… That is, I wasn’t really thinking about…’ She huffed out a breath. ‘It’s quite cheeky to slip into people’s minds and steal their thoughts, you know.’

events.did: 说「我真的不觉得你尝起来像焦糖和盐。我根本不想尝你。」热浪冲上脸颊，怀疑自己会不会尴尬而死——那会给上议院省不少麻烦；「那只是一个跑偏的念头。就像蜜蜂在蜂巢里有没有朋友。」
events.verbatim: ‘I don’t really think you taste of caramel and salt. I don’t want to taste you at any rate.’ Heat washed Cynthia’s cheeks, and she wondered if it was possible to die from embarrassment. It would save the House of Lords a lot of trouble. ‘It was just one of those errant thoughts. Like whether bees have friends in their hive.’

events.did: 铜色眉毛抬起，灰眼变成银色（一定是阳光把戏）；反问「你在想蜜蜂有没有朋友？」
events.verbatim: Helena’s copper brows rose as her grey eyes shifted to silver. It must be a trick of sunlight. ‘You wonder if bees have friends?’

events.did: 门开了，两人同时弹开；海伦娜抓起另一封信，辛西娅把鼻子埋回账簿
events.verbatim: The door opened. They both jerked apart. Helena grabbed for another letter as Cynthia buried her nose back in the ledger.

events.did: 说「我追了那杂种二十个街区。他在七钟区甩掉我。那里的街道就是个该死的迷宫。那个偷偷摸摸的小混蛋！」他一向略显凌乱，这次是全新级别的混乱：深褐色卷发到处支棱、双颊热得绯红、裤脚滴着泥；问「你们打开保险箱了？」目光从辛西娅扫到海伦娜，再扫到从保险箱倒出的东西
events.verbatim: ‘I chased the bastard for twenty blocks. He lost me in the Seven Dials. The streets there are like a bloody maze. The sneaky little shite!’ Superintendent MacDougal always looked slightly dishevelled, but this was an entirely new level of chaos. Dark-brown curls stuck out in every direction. His cheeks were a hectic crimson, and the bottom of his trousers dripped with mud. ‘You opened the safe?’ His sharp gaze flicked from Cynthia to Helena, then to the contents spilling from the safe.

events.did: 说「是我的主意」，不想再给海伦娜一个不信任自己的理由；「布莱尔小姐想等你回来，但我想保险箱里也许有能开脱我的东西，所以是我坚持的」；她笨拙地站起来，左脚麻了
events.verbatim: ‘It was my idea.’ Cynthia didn’t need to give Helena another reason to mistrust her. ‘Miss Blair wanted to wait until your return, but I thought there might be something in Hubert’s safe to absolve me, so I insisted.’ Cynthia stood awkwardly. Her left foot had fallen asleep.

events.did: 从手里的纸抬头又低头看羊皮纸，嘴巴无声地吸气
events.verbatim: Helena looked up from the paper in her hands then back again at the parchment. Her mouth opened in a silent inhalation.

events.did: 问「你没事吧，姑娘？」
events.verbatim: ‘Are ye well, lass?’

events.did: 说「我想我找到了。」
events.verbatim: ‘I think I found it.’

events.who: 辛西娅与麦克杜格尔警司
events.did: 同时问「什么？」
events.verbatim: ‘What?’ Cynthia and Superintendent MacDougal spoke together.

events.did: 说「能证明辛西娅无罪的证据」；叙述者点出这是海伦娜第一次用辛西娅的名字——词还没处理完，麻刺般的战栗已冲过她的皮肤
events.verbatim: ‘The evidence to exonerate Cynthia.’ It was the first time Helena used Cynthia’s name. Tingles washed over her skin before she processed the words that came before her name.

events.did: 伸手去拿纸、从海伦娜手里抢走：「证据？」海伦娜抱怨着从地上爬起来，哈姆雷特在两人之间穿梭、尾巴拖着掠过辛西娅的裙子、头撞上海伦娜的大腿，但她几乎没注意
events.verbatim: ‘Evidence?’ She reached for the paper and snatched it out of Helena’s hands. ‘Hey!’ Helena sputtered as she regained her feet. Hamlet wound between the two of them, his tail trailing over Cynthia’s skirt in a whisper as his head bumped into Helena’s thigh. But she barely noticed.

events.did: 羊皮纸上的字迹粗犷 stark，与文字一样有力
events.verbatim: The script written on thick parchment was as bold and stark as the words.

events.did: 「期限已过。履行你的契约，或全额偿还你的债务。违背与魔鬼的约定会带来深远的后果。」——本章末句
events.verbatim: The deadline has passed. Fulfil your bargain or pay your debt in full. Breaking a deal with the Devil carries profound consequences.

traps_noted: L56「Aunt Rowan’s was a fifteen-minute walk from their cottage in the woods」——是「罗恩姨妈家」，不是罗恩姨妈本人；小屋在林子里
L62「pulled the water from the air」＝从空气中抽水；「a wave of power」＝力量之浪，不是「水流之浪」的实写
L68「destroyed her entire world」＝倾诉本身摧毁了她的世界，不含具体后果描述
L101 说话者是拉奇兰叔叔（苏格兰方言），他自称以「苏格兰场警长」身份说话；麦克杜格尔是另一个警官（Superintendent MacDougal）——两者不可混为一人
L122 麦克杜格尔警司与海伦娜是叔侄
L146「I asked him to help pack Hubert’s things」＝辛西娅请男仆帮忙收拾遗物
L158「poorly fitting suit hiding his shape」＝窃贼身形被不合身西装遮住；男仆坐在地上被绑
L164 窃贼心中的「The Devil」＝他害怕的雇主/契约对象（与章末羊皮纸同源线索），不是指辛西娅本人——但不得断言
L176 海伦娜的水浪「inadvertently aiding his escape」＝本想阻止反而助其逃脱
L194 辛西娅先称哈姆雷特为「a lovely fox」，被龇牙后改口「a wild and fearsome creature」——两句都在原文，不可只取其一
L212 男仆原话是「He could have killed you both」
L269 白兰地那句是辛西娅对哈姆雷特说完「Mr Higgins」式插话后补的（Brandy can also be quite restorative）
L291 DOSD 是账簿上反复出现的字母组合，非人名拼写
L321「新门监狱（Newgate）」是监狱名，不是「新城门」
L330「I don’t want you to be guilty」是海伦娜的话；同段「a woman’s lips were softer」是辛西娅的疑问
L354 海伦娜的灰眼「shifted to silver」，叙述者解释为「It must be a trick of sunlight」——不是施法
L378 海伦娜第一次叫「辛西娅」的名字
L396 羊皮纸四句是正文（未加引号），属契约文本
